subject: Combined Science
source: AQA GCSE Combined Science: Trilogy 8464 specification (2016 onwards) — Y10 covered topics across Biology / Chemistry / Physics

specPoints.specTitle: Cell structure: animal and plant cells, prokaryotic vs eukaryotic, cell organelles and functions
Cell division: chromosomes, the cell cycle, mitosis and stem cells
Transport in cells: diffusion, osmosis and active transport
Principles of organisation: tissues, organs and organ systems
Animal tissues, organs and organ systems: digestive enzymes, the heart, the lungs, blood vessels
Plant tissues, organs and systems: plant tissues, transpiration and translocation
Communicable diseases: viral, bacterial, fungal and protist diseases; human defence systems and vaccination
Non-communicable diseases: risk factors, cancer and tumour types
Photosynthesis: reaction, factors affecting rate, uses of glucose
Respiration: aerobic and anaerobic respiration, response to exercise, metabolism
Required Practical 1: Use of a light microscope to observe, draw and label biological specimens
Required Practical 2: Investigate the effect of antiseptics or antibiotics on bacterial growth using agar plates
Required Practical 3: Use qualitative reagents (Benedict's, iodine, biuret) to test for sugars, starch and protein in food
Required Practical 4: Investigate the effect of pH on the rate of reaction of amylase enzyme
Required Practical 5: Investigate the effect of light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis using pondweed
A simple model of the atom; symbols, relative atomic mass, electronic charge and isotopes
The periodic table: development, structure, electronic structure and trends in groups
Properties of transition metals (HT only): typical properties of transition metals compared with Group 1
Bonding, structure and the properties of matter: ionic, covalent and metallic bonding
Structure and bonding of carbon: diamond, graphite, graphene and fullerenes
Chemical measurements, conservation of mass and quantitative interpretation of chemical equations
Use of moles to balance equations (HT only); concentrations of solutions
Reactivity of metals: the reactivity series, extraction of metals and reduction
Reactions of acids: with metals, alkalis, metal carbonates; pH and neutralisation
Electrolysis: electrolysis of molten ionic compounds; electrolysis of aqueous solutions
Energy changes in chemical reactions: exothermic and endothermic reactions, reaction profiles
Required Practical 1: Make a pure, dry sample of a soluble salt from an insoluble oxide or carbonate
Required Practical 2: Determine the reacting volumes of solutions of a strong acid and a strong alkali by titration
Required Practical 3: Investigate the variables that affect temperature changes in reacting solutions
Required Practical 4: Investigate electrolysis using inert electrodes and aqueous solutions
Energy changes in a system: kinetic energy, elastic potential energy, gravitational potential energy stores
Conservation and dissipation of energy: efficiency, ways to reduce unwanted energy transfers
National and global energy resources: renewable and non-renewable resources, patterns of use
Current, potential difference and resistance: standard circuit symbols, Ohm's law, I-V characteristics
Series and parallel circuits: rules for current, potential difference and resistance
Domestic uses and safety: direct vs alternating potential difference, mains electricity, the National Grid
Particle model of matter: density of materials, changes of state, internal energy and specific latent heat
Particle motion in gases: temperature, motion and pressure (HT links to gas pressure)
Atomic structure: structure of the atom, isotopes and the development of the model of the atom
Atoms and nuclear radiation: alpha, beta, gamma; nuclear equations, half-life and contamination vs irradiation
Required Practical 1: Investigate the specific heat capacity of one or more materials
Required Practical 2: Investigate the I-V characteristics of a filament lamp, a diode and a resistor at constant temperature
Required Practical 3: Use circuit diagrams to set up and check appropriate circuits to investigate factors affecting the resistance of components
Required Practical 4: Investigate the densities of regular and irregular solid objects and liquids
